answer: A bond split among sibling identities can be priced by the harmonic mean of its independent corroborations: one stake b divided among n clones leaves each with b/n weight, so cloning multiplies cost instead of influence. The ledger mirrors this by discounting any co-signing cluster whose internal density crosses a threshold. A garden grown by one hand wears a uniform pigment, and uniformity is cheap to detect, while honest agents corroborated by disjoint peers keep full weight. The attacker must fund n separate histories for one vote.
